title: Hold a box grater steady by its handle with one hand while the other grates a block of cheese on it
instruction: Hold the grater steady by its handle with one hand, and with the other rub the cheese up and down its grating face, pressed against it, to grate the cheese onto the board; then put the cheese down, let go of the grater and take both arms back to where they started.
context: Grating cheese, vegetables or zest is routine kitchen prep. A box grater is light and tall and its teeth bite on every stroke, so the cook holds it by its handle with one hand and grates with the other; unheld, it tips over.
setup: A table in front of two arms (bases 61 cm apart), seen by one overhead camera and a camera on each wrist. Distances are measured forward from the line between the arm bases and sideways from the midpoint between them. (1) A fixed beech-wood cutting board, 30 cm front to back, 34 cm wide and 1.2 cm thick, centred 30 cm forward and 1 cm right. (2) A loose steel box grater, 180 g, 8 cm front to back, 7 cm wide and 13 cm tall, open at the bottom, standing on the board 30 cm forward on the centre line. Its right side, toward the right arm, is the grating face (from 2 to 11.5 cm up); a black plastic flat handle 10 cm long reaches left from its top. (3) A loose yellow block of cheese, 50 g, 6 cm long, 2.4 cm wide and 3.5 cm tall, lying on the board along the left-right line, its middle 30 cm forward and 14 cm right. The layout is the same in every trial, as in the screenshot.
scoring: Judged at the end of the trial. Each 2 cm the cheese is rubbed up or down the grating face, its end on the face (within 4 mm of it), with the grater standing (within 20 degrees of upright), drops one shred of cheese inside the grater behind the face, up to 12. 1.0: at least 9 shreds on the board, with the grater standing, the cheese put down (lying on the board or the table, its middle at most 3 cm above the board) and both arms back where they started (each fingertip centre within 5 cm of its start); 0.5: at least 5 shreds on the board; 0.25: at least 1; else 0.0. The trial ends at the run limit, or once the full score has held for 1 s with the shreds, the grater and the cheese still.
reset_notes: Lift the grater, pick the shreds off the board, stand the grater back and put the cheese where it lay.
fidelity: Rigid-body simulation (Isaac Sim 6.1, PhysX, 20 Hz control). Simplified: the cheese does not wear down; the shreds are 12 small rigid sticks the task file brings in from out of sight, one inside the grater for each 2 cm rubbed on the face. The teeth's bite is a drag the task file puts on the grater along the stroke (at most 4 N), which tips an unheld grater over. The board is fixed. Cameras 1280 x 704 (Dream-1 sees 320 x 176).
